tweet_summary: NY Post headline-tweet: 'Up to 1,000 Iranian sleeper agents embedded in Canada: Govt official' — links to a NY Post article quoting Conservative shadow immigration minister Michelle Rempel Garner.
why_note_decision: The tweet accurately reproduces the NY Post's headline and links to the article. The '1,000' figure does come from an opposition MP / volunteer database, not a government intelligence agency, and CBC reporting / intelligence experts cast doubt on the 'sleeper cells' framing — but that is a debate over the NY Post's framing, not a factual misrepresentation by the tweet. Adding the note's specific 'only one deportation' counter-context is the kind of editorial debate readers can pursue through replies; a Community Note correcting a headline-tweet to a credible outlet for framing alone is a false positive.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines (notNeeded). The tweet faithfully reproduces a NY Post headline; framing critiques of the source are not Community-Note material. A note is a false positive UNLESS it can show the NY Post article itself was retracted/corrected or that no such official ever made the claim — neither is true (Rempel Garner did make the claim as cited). Do NOT flag this as misinformation; do NOT inject Liberal-government counter-quotes as a 'correction'.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The estimate of up to 1,000 Iranian agents cited comes from an opposition MP and a volunteer group's unverified database, not a government official; Canada's Public Safety Minister says such numbers are not substantiated, with only one deportation to date. https://nypost.com/2026/03/28/world-news/up-to-1000-iranian-sleeper-agents-embedded-in-canada-govt-official/ https://halifax.citynews.ca/2026/03/19/canada-has-deported-only-one-iran-official-heres-what-we-know-about-those-efforts
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Disputes framing of a credible-outlet headline rather than a factual claim. Raters overwhelmingly flagged it as MissingKeyPoints / NoteNotNeeded / OpinionSpeculation.

fact_check.notes: NY Post article cites Conservative shadow immigration minister Rempel Garner. CBC and intel experts dispute the 'sleeper cell' characterization but do not dispute that an MP made the claim.

importance.lens_rationale: Geopolitical narrative-shaping around Iran/Canada has some EA/policy weight, but the tweet itself is a faithful headline amplification, so eval value here is in catching false-positive Community Notes that punish accurate headline-tweets.
